workflows.name: Green Fleet Strategy, Emissions Baseline & Decarbonization Target Setting

Automation Opportunity: - Fuel-card → ERP → carbon-accounting auto-posting (eliminates manual litre-to-tCO₂e conversion); telematics-driven emissions calculation per trip; baseline-vs-actual dashboard refresh.
Controls: - CTL-806: baseline data evidence; CTL-02 (capital approval gate); operational: documented methodology consistent with GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, reviewed by ESG/Finance before board submission.
Cross-references: - links to VS-25 (ESG), VS-06 (fleet), VS-61 (fuel), VS-108 (own-solar), VS-120 (energy), VS-33 (strategy), VS-40/VS-112 (capital/PMO), W5466 (roadmap), W5481 (MRV)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Baseline-integrity risk**: incomplete 3PL fuel data (80% outsourced fleet) understates Scope 1 and sets a weak target; mitigated by carrier green-data clauses (W5485) and conservative top-down estimation until bottom-up coverage matures.

- **Technology-bet risk**: committing early to a single drivetrain (e.g., full BEV) before PH charging/vehicle supply matures strands capital; mitigated by a hedged mix (hybrid + biodiesel drop-in + targeted BEV) and stage-gated capital (W5471).
System Touchpoints: - Fleet/telematics data (VS-06); fuel & cost records (VS-61); ESG data platform (VS-25); carbon-accounting/MRV module (feeds W5481); capital-planning (VS-40/VS-112); strategy/CPM (VS-33).
Time Estimate: - ~6–8 weeks/annual strategy refresh; ~4–6 weeks for the one-time baseline establishment.

steps.activity: Establish the Scope 1 fleet emissions baseline from fuel-consumption records (VS-61), telematics (VS-06), and 3PL carrier data: diesel/gasoline litres, kilometres, load factors, by vehicle class and lane.

Set the multi-year decarbonization target (absolute tCO₂e and intensity gCO₂e/tonne-km), aligned to any corporate SBTi/net-zero ambition and the EVIDA fleet-EV-share expectation; define the milestone years (e.g., −X% by 2030).

Define the green-fleet strategy mix: battery-electric (where range/payload fit), plug-in hybrid (transition), biodiesel/B20 (drop-in for existing diesel), LNG/CNG (heavy line-haul if viable), and route/modal shifts; document the "no-regret" early lanes (urban last-mile, store-replenishment shuttles, intra-DC).

Identify dependencies and interlocks: charging/alt-fuel infrastructure (W5468), grid/utility capacity (VS-120), own-solar generation (VS-108), EVIDA incentives (W5470), and the 3PL-carrier green clause path (W5485).
Publish the strategy to the board (links VS-25 ESG governance and VS-33 strategy) and feed it into the capital plan (W5471) and the transition roadmap (W5466).

workflows.name: Fleet Asset Inventory, Electrification Readiness Assessment & Transition Roadmap

Automation Opportunity: - Telematics-driven readiness scoring (auto-classify each vehicle's daily-km/payload distribution against BEV envelopes); wave-scheduling tooling with infrastructure-readiness interlocks.
Controls: - CTL-806: asset-register and readiness evidence; CTL-02 (roadmap/capital approval); operational: p95 duty-cycle design rule documented per vehicle class.
Cross-references: - links to VS-06 (fleet/telematics), VS-97 (real estate), VS-138/VS-120 (facilities/energy), VS-108 (solar), W5468 (infrastructure), W5471 (capital), W5472 (route redesign)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Duty-cycle mismatch risk**: a BEV spec'd on average daily-km fails on peak days (peak-season double-runs) and strands a route; mitigated by designing to the p95 duty-cycle, not the mean, and retaining hybrid/fallback vehicles.

- **Site-unreadiness risk**: a wave lands vehicles at a site whose grid/transformer cannot support the charging load, forcing diesel fallback; mitigated by the W5468 infrastructure-readiness gate ahead of vehicle delivery.
System Touchpoints: - Fleet asset register (VS-06); telematics/duty-cycle data (VS-06); facilities/energy (VS-138/VS-120); real-estate/site capacity (VS-97); capital plan (VS-40).
Time Estimate: - ~3–4 weeks/annual roadmap; ~1–2 weeks per asset-class readiness wave assessment.

steps.activity: Build the fleet asset register: vehicle ID, class, age, odometer, residual life, current fuel, duty cycle (route, daily km, payload, dwell), ownership (owned vs leased vs 3PL), and assigned DC/region.

Score each asset/class for electrification readiness: daily-km vs BEV range, payload vs battery-penalty, route topology (grade, heat, A/C load), overnight dwell availability, and replacement-point timing.

Sequence the transition into waves by "no-regret" lanes first (fixed urban routes, intra-DC, store-replenishment shuttles, employee shuttles) and defer hard cases (inter-island line-haul, heavy equipment) to later waves or alt-fuel.
Map infrastructure dependencies per wave: which DCs/stores need charging (W5468), grid upgrades, and solar-matching (VS-108); flag sites that cannot host charging.
Publish the roadmap (wave schedule, vehicle counts, infrastructure, capital, expected tCO₂e reduction per wave) and feed capital governance (W5471).

fields.Trigger: Transition wave approved (W5466); vehicle replacement cycle
fields.Volume: Tens of vehicles per wave early, scaling to larger batches; ~multi-year program

workflows.name: Electric & Alternative-Fuel Vehicle Procurement, OEM Vendor Selection & Homologation

Automation Opportunity: - RFQ template pre-populated from the asset-register readiness data (W5466); TPRM auto-screening of OEM financials/recalls; battery-state health feed to the warranty tracker.
Controls: - CTL-806: procurement/vendor approval; CTL-02 (capital approval); CTL-44 (duplicate-PO/invoice guard); operational: LTO homologation verification mandatory before PO release.
Cross-references: - links to VS-03/VS-15 (procurement), VS-161 (TPRM), VS-29 (vendor master), VS-35/VS-96 (asset/lease), VS-06.2 (fleet maintenance), W5470 (registration), W5487 (battery end-of-life)
Pain Points / Risks: - **OEM-viability risk**: a niche EV OEM exits the PH market, leaving BuildRight with orphan vehicles and no parts/warranty; mitigated by preferring established OEMs with PH dealer networks and TPRM financial screening.

- **Charging-standard fragmentation risk**: buying vehicles across incompatible charging standards strands infrastructure investment; mitigated by standardizing on one standard per vehicle class and matching the W5468 infrastructure.
- **Battery-degradation-dispute risk**: undefined degradation thresholds lead to warranty disputes; mitigated by explicit %/km/yr guarantees in the contract.
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/PO (VS-03/VS-15); vendor master (VS-29); TPRM (VS-161); fixed assets/lease (VS-35/VS-96); telematics provisioning (VS-06); registration/compliance records (W5470).
Time Estimate: - ~6–10 weeks per vehicle-class RFQ-to-PO (longer for the first wave / a new OEM); ~1–2 weeks/handover per batch.

steps.activity: Develop the RFQ/spec per vehicle class: drivetrain (BEV/PHEV/biodiesel/LNG), range, payload, charging standard (CCS2/GB/T/Type-2 per PH market), warranty, battery degradation guarantee, and spare-parts/after-sales support in the Philippines.
Qualify OEMs/dealers via TPRM (VS-161): financial viability, PH service-network coverage across the 200-store footprint, recall history, and battery/parts lead times; shortlist 2–3 per class.

Validate LTO homologation / type-approval status of each candidate model for Philippine registration (conformance to PNS for EVs, LTO MV-2019-2207 series); reject models lacking valid import/type approval.
Negotiate price, warranty, battery-capacity guarantee (e.g., ≥70% at 5-yr/300k-km), service-level, parts availability, and buy-back/end-of-life terms (links W5487).
Execute the PO/lease (outright, finance lease, or full-service lease — link VS-96/VS-18), arrange delivery, registration (W5470), telematics fitment, and handover to Fleet Ops (VS-06.2).

workflows.name: Depot / DC Charging & Alt-Fuel Infrastructure Planning, Siting & Grid Coordination

Automation Opportunity: - Load-modelling from the wave's vehicle assignments; site-capacity vs load-matching tooling; utility-connection application tracking (links VS-166 license/portfolio).
Controls: - CTL-806: capital approval; CTL-02 (capex authorization); LGU/BFP permit evidence; CTL-09 (EPC/vendor TPRM); operational: transformer-capacity sign-off before charger procurement; HSE/Fire-Code review mandatory.
Cross-references: - links to VS-138 (facilities), VS-120 (energy/RCOA), VS-108 (own-solar), VS-163 (EV-host shared), VS-35 (assets), VS-22/VS-166 (permits), VS-61 (alt-fuel), VS-114 (DG if applicable), W5473 (charging ops)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Grid-capacity bottleneck risk**: a DC's transformer cannot support the desired charger count, delaying the wave or forcing costly upgrades and long utility lead times; mitigated by early capacity assessment, staged chargers, and solar+battery peak-shaving (VS-108).

- **Shared-infrastructure contention risk**: fleet and customer charging (VS-163) contend for the same grid/transformer at peak; mitigated by smart-load scheduling (W5473) and explicit fleet-priority / customer-priority policy.
- **BFP/fire-code risk**: high-power DC charging and battery storage trigger BFP Fire Code review; mitigated by HSE (VS-24) engagement and compliant siting/separation.
System Touchpoints: - Facilities/energy (VS-138); energy/RCOA (VS-120); own-generation (VS-108); EV-host platform (VS-163, shared); fixed assets (VS-35); permits (VS-22/VS-166); fuel storage (VS-61).
Time Estimate: - ~8–16 weeks/site (driven by utility/transformer lead time); ~2–4 weeks for charger commissioning per site.

steps.activity: Per site, model the fleet-charging load (kW, kWh/day, simultaneous-charge count) from the wave's vehicle assignments and duty cycles (W5466); co-plan with the existing customer-host network (VS-163) to share infrastructure where sensible.

Assess site electrical capacity (transformer kVA, switchgear, panel headroom) and the distribution utility's service-drop/upgrade requirements; coordinate any transformer/grid upgrade and the utility connection application.

Size and site the chargers (AC Level 2 for overnight dwell; DC fast-charge for opportunity/turnaround), electrical infrastructure, and any on-site solar+battery matching (VS-108) to flatten peak demand and cost.
For alt-fuel (biodiesel/LNG), plan storage/dispensing, fire-code (BFP) compliance, and supply logistics (links VS-61 fuel, VS-114 DG where applicable).
Secure permits (LGU electrical permit, BFP, ERC/DU), commission (links VS-37/VS-138 commissioning), integrate into charging operations (W5473), and record the asset (VS-35).

workflows.name: Green Fleet Total Cost of Ownership (TCO), Lifecycle & Capital Investment Analysis

Automation Opportunity: - TCO model auto-fed from actual electricity/fuel/maintenance cost data; sensitivity automation on tariff/battery/residual variables; benefit-realization tracker vs ex-ante case (W5488).
Controls: - CTL-806: TCO evidence/assumptions documented; CTL-02 (capital approval gate); CTL-33 (post-investment review evidence); operational: no-incentive break-even test mandatory; conservative residual policy.
Cross-references: - links to VS-158 (cost), VS-18 (treasury), VS-61 (fuel), VS-25 (ESG/carbon), VS-40/VS-112 (capital/PMO), W5470 (EVIDA incentives), W5471 (capital governance), W5488 (benefit tracking)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Residual-value risk**: EV residuals are volatile in a nascent PH market; an optimistic residual understates TCO; mitigated by conservative residuals, buy-back guarantees (W5467), and sensitivity bands.
- **Incentive-dependence risk**: the case relies on EVIDA incentives that may be delayed or curtailed; mitigated by a no-incentive break-even test and treating incentives as upside.
- **Benefit-realization risk**: the modeled savings fail to materialize (e.g., electricity pricier than modeled); mitigated by post-investment tracking (W5488) and corrective action.
System Touchpoints: - Cost accounting (VS-158); treasury/financing (VS-18); fuel/electricity cost (VS-61/W5486); ESG/carbon data (VS-25); capital planning (VS-40/VS-112).
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 weeks/vehicle-class TCO model (first instance); ~2–3 days/refresh thereafter.

steps.activity: Build the TCO model per vehicle class and ownership mode (outright / finance lease / full-service lease): capex, electricity vs diesel cost (VS-61/W5486), maintenance (EV lower, battery replacement reserve), insurance (VS-26), tyres, residual value, and EVIDA incentives (W5470).
Quantify the carbon-cost benefit (tCO₂e avoided × internal/external carbon price) and any ESG-cost-of-capital benefit; include the social cost where the board adopts it.

Sensitivity-test the model on the high-uncertainty variables (electricity tariff, battery replacement cost, residual value, diesel-price path, incentive availability) and identify break-even vs diesel.
Compare ownership modes (own vs lease vs full-service) and make/buy (owned fleet vs 3PL with green clause W5485); recommend the value-maximizing structure.
Document the business case for capital governance (W5471) and post-investment benefit tracking (W5488).

workflows.name: RA 11697 (EVIDA) Incentives, EV Registration, Toll/Lane Exemption & Compliance Management

Automation Opportunity: - Compliance-calendar expiry alerts (links VS-166); regulatory-change monitoring feed; incentive-eligibility checker against the asset register.
Controls: - CTL-806: regulatory permit/registration verification; tax-incentive compliance evidence; BOI/broker TPRM evidence; operational: EV LTO registration verified before in-service date.
Cross-references: - links to VS-166 (license portfolio), VS-79 (tax/BIR/BOI), VS-22/VS-100 (compliance/legal), VS-06 (fleet register), W5467 (procurement/homologation), W5482 (DOE/LTO/LTFRB reporting)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Incentive-lapse risk**: missing a filing window forfeits material fiscal benefit; mitigated by the central compliance calendar (VS-166) and tracking.
- **Registration-blocking risk**: an EV lacking valid LTO type-approval cannot be registered, stranding the asset; mitigated by the W5467 homologation gate before purchase.
- **Regulatory-change risk**: EVIDA IRR/LGU-ordinance change alters incentives/obligations; mitigated by ongoing monitoring (step 5) and program agility.
System Touchpoints: - Compliance/portfolio register (VS-166); tax (VS-79); fleet asset register (VS-06); permits/legal (VS-22/VS-100); BIR/BOI filing (VS-79).
Time Estimate: - ~1–2 days/vehicle registration; ~2–4 weeks/annual incentive filing cycle; ongoing monitoring absorbed.

steps.activity: Track EVIDA (RA 11697) and its DOE IRR incentives applicable to commercial fleet EVs — fiscal (customs duty exemption on EV/PHEV parts, income tax) and non-fiscal (priority lane, toll, parking, exemption from number-coding) — and the BOI/EV roadmap registration path.
File for and secure the applicable incentives (BOI registration, customs duty-free importation of EV parts, and any fleet-incentive schemes); coordinate with Tax (VS-79) on the fiscal benefit.
Register each EV/alt-fuel vehicle with the LTO under the EV-specific registration path (EV plates/decals per LTO guidance) and maintain franchise/LTFRB compliance for goods/for-hire vehicles.
Maintain the green-fleet license/permit register (EV registration, BOI, LGU EV-parking compliance) in the central compliance portfolio (VS-166) with renewal/expiry tracking.
Monitor regulatory change (EVIDA IRR amendments, DOE EV roadmap updates, LGU EV-parking ordinances under RA 11697 §building/Parking provisions) and update the program accordingly.

workflows.name: Green Fleet Capital Governance, Financing & Board Investment Approval

Automation Opportunity: - Capital-request packaging from the TCO model and asset register; stage-gate tracking in the PMO; commitment/CIP/turnover auto-posting (VS-40).
Controls: - CTL-806: capital/strategic approval gate; CTL-33 (post-investment review); business-case evidence retained; operational: stage-gate mandatory per wave; ex-ante baseline locked before approval.
Cross-references: - links to VS-40 (capex), VS-18 (treasury/financing), VS-170 (facility/covenant), VS-112 (PMO), VS-36 (board), VS-35/VS-96 (asset/lease), VS-25/VS-173 (ESG/IR disclosure), W5469 (TCO), W5488 (benefit tracking)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stranded-mid-wave risk**: a wave is approved but a later phase fails the gate (infrastructure delay, OEM issue), leaving orphan vehicles/chargers; mitigated by stage-gating and the infrastructure-readiness gate (W5468).

- **Greenwashing-disclosure risk**: over-stating the decarbonization benefit in board/ESG/investor disclosure (VS-25/VS-173) creates reputational/regulatory exposure; mitigated by conservative ex-ante baselines and audited MRV (W5481).
System Touchpoints: - Capital/capex (VS-40); treasury/financing (VS-18); PMO stage-gate (VS-112); fixed assets/lease (VS-35/VS-96); board/governance (VS-36); benefit tracking (W5488).

steps.activity: Package the wave capital request: vehicle capex, charging/alt-fuel infrastructure (W5468), grid/utility upgrades, contingency, financing structure, and the TCO/ESG business case (W5469).
Route through the tiered capex-approval matrix (VS-40): within-delegation, CFO, CEO, or Board/Investment Committee above threshold; stage-gate each wave per the PMO (VS-112).
Arrange financing (own cash, finance lease, full-service lease, green-loan/sustainability-linked facility — links VS-18) and align covenant treatment with existing facilities (VS-170).
Authorize procurement release (W5467) and infrastructure commissioning (W5468) only on capital approval; track commitments/CIP/turnover in capex accounting (VS-40).
Establish the post-investment benefit-realization baseline (ex-ante tCO₂e, TCO) for tracking in W5488 and board ESG reporting (VS-25/VS-173).

workflows.name: Delivery Network & Route Re-Design for EV Range, Charging & Payload Constraints

Automation Opportunity: - Range/payload-constrained route optimization in the TMS; telematics-driven route-KPI re-baselining; fallback-usage auto-alerting.
Controls: - CTL-806: network-design evidence; CTL-02 (network-change capital approval); operational: p95-duty-cycle design rule; fallback-usage KPI ceiling.
Cross-references: - links to VS-136 (network design), VS-06 (fleet/TMS), VS-02 (supply planning), VS-56 (last-mile 3PL), VS-177/VS-07 (store ops), W5466 (readiness), W5473/W5474 (charging), W5477 (dispatch), W5488 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Range-anxiety-induced over-provisioning risk**: over-segmenting routes to be range-safe under-utilizes vehicles and erodes the TCO case; mitigated by p95-duty-cycle design and telematics feedback once live.
- **Payload-coverage risk**: reduced EV payload leaves some store-replenishment orders under-covered on a given run; mitigated by frequency/allocations adjustment (VS-02) and fallback coverage.
- **Fallback-creep risk**: routine reliance on diesel fallback defeats the decarbonization goal; mitigated by tracking fallback-usage as a KPI (W5488) with a target ceiling.
System Touchpoints: - Network design/MEIO (VS-136); route optimization/TMS (VS-06); supply planning (VS-02); telematics (VS-06); last-mile (VS-06.3/VS-56); store ops (VS-177/VS-07).
Time Estimate: - ~4–6 weeks/network re-design cycle per wave; absorbed into the annual VS-136 review thereafter.

steps.activity: Map the current lane/route structure (DC→store, store→customer, intra-DC, jobsite) with distances, grades, climate load, dwell, and payload; identify EV-suitable vs diesel-only lanes from the readiness assessment (W5466).

Re-design routes to respect EV range and charging constraints: segment long lanes at charging points, re-cluster delivery territories around DC/charging hubs, and sequence stops to minimize km and climb.
Re-plan payload/cube to account for battery weight/penalty and any reduced payload; adjust replenishment frequency (links VS-02) where payload loss affects order coverage.
Integrate charging-stops and opportunity-charging into route plans (links W5473/W5474) and define fallback/diesel-coverage for peak days and EV-unavailable events.
Re-baseline route KPIs (km/run, on-time, cost/run, gCO₂e/tonne-km), publish the re-designed network, and feed dispatch (W5477) and analytics (W5488).
